FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only deliverable — no experiment executed, no results claimed)

TITLE
Effect of a chemical property-feedback loop on molecule quality, hallucination, and structural diversity in targeted molecule discovery: a controlled two-arm experiment.

1. SETUP

1.1 Two-arm controlled comparison
- Arm A (baseline): base generator samples molecules unconditionally (no property feedback).
- Arm B (feedback): identical generator with a property-feedback loop layered on top. The ONLY difference between arms is feedback on/off.
- Matched factors (fixed requirements): identical random seed(s), identical model capacity and checkpoint/weights, identical sampling budget (same number of raw generations per arm), identical chemistry toolkit and scoring pipeline version.

1.2 Base generator [ASSUMPTION — not source-specified]
Assumption: a SMILES-based generative model (e.g., a small pre-trained autoregressive SMILES model such as a MolGPT-style/character-level transformer, or a conditional VAE) serves as the base. The design is agnostic to the framework; any generator that (a) can sample N molecules deterministically given a seed and (b) accepts external guidance (rejection sampling or reward re-weighting) qualifies. Selection criterion stated in design: simplest framework that runs CPU-only offline.

1.3 Feedback mechanism [ASSUMPTION — not source-specified]
Assumption — operational definition of the chemical feedback loop:
- Loop: generate batch → score each molecule on three properties → compute composite reward → feed back via re-weighting/rejection (generate k candidate batches, keep/resample with probability proportional to reward) → repeat for T feedback iterations.
- Reward: R = w1·norm(p-logP) + w2·QED + w3·norm(affinity_surrogate), where norm(·) maps each property to [0,1] against the reference set's empirical quantiles (this prevents degenerate rewards like infinite logP).
- Property definitions [ASSUMPTION]: p-logP = penalized cLogP (cLogP − ring count penalty − too-long-chain penalty, the standard penalized-logP form); QED = RDKit quantitative estimate of drug-likeness ∈ [0,1]; binding affinity = affinity surrogate (see 1.4).
- Feedback strength sweep: run Arm B at multiple feedback strengths (e.g., soft re-weighting β ∈ {low, medium, high}, where β scales reward sharpness) — this exposes the diversity–property trade-off rather than a single point estimate. T (iterations) [ASSUMPTION]: small fixed grid, e.g., T ∈ {1, 5}, to test whether more feedback iterations worsen collapse.
- Weights w1=w2=w3=1 [ASSUMPTION]; a sensitivity check with alternate weights is included.

1.4 Affinity surrogate [ASSUMPTION — no receptor specified in any source]
Assumption: binding affinity is approximated by a fixed, pre-computed surrogate — either (i) a pre-trained affinity predictor applied to all candidates, or (ii) docking scores against ONE fixed common target protein held constant across both arms. Critical: the surrogate/target must be identical in both arms so it cancels out of the A/B comparison. Results are proxy-relative only (see Limitations).

2. CONTROLS

- Matched compute/sampling budget: both arms draw the same number of raw generated molecules and the same number of scoring calls (feedback arm's resampling counts against its budget — no free extra samples).
- Same reference set: both arms evaluated against the SAME real-world reference dataset [ASSUMPTION: a standard public drug-like collection, e.g., a ChEMBL- or ZINC-derived filtered set; reference sampling protocol: random subsample of size n_ref specified in the design, same for all comparisons].
- Same scoring pipeline: one scoring script computes p-logP, QED, affinity surrogate, validity, uniqueness, OOD, diversity for BOTH arms — eliminating pipeline-induced asymmetry.
- Same seed protocol: N seeds (e.g., 5) per arm; each seed produces a paired (A_i, B_i) sample for paired statistics. Same seeds used in both arms so pair i shares initialization.
- Isolation of the factor under test: only the feedback flag differs; identical post-processing (deterministic canonicalization, no arm-specific filtering).
- Negative/positive sanity control [ASSUMPTION, optional if budget allows]: a third arm with a "flipped" reward (maximize chain length) to confirm the pipeline can detect diversity degradation when induced deliberately — validating the metrics are sensitive, not just null.

3. METRICS (full distributions for everything; means reported only alongside IQRs/full CDFs)

3.1 Property scores
- p-logP, QED, affinity surrogate: computed per molecule; reported as full empirical distributions (violin/CDF + quantiles), per arm, with paired differences per seed.
- Validity-adjusted property gains: property metrics computed ONLY on valid molecules, AND reported as budget-level aggregate = (mean property over valid molecules) × (validity rate), so a feedback arm cannot win by generating invalid-but-scored-favorably outputs. Both views reported.

3.2 Hallucination metrics (three components per researcher refinement)
- (a) Validity rate: fraction of generated SMILES that parse and pass RDKit valence/sanitization.
- (b) Out-of-distribution (OOD) rate: fraction of generated molecules outside the reference real-world distribution [ASSUMPTION: operationalized as (i) nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity to reference set below a threshold AND (ii) multivariate property-vector outlier via distance to reference quantiles; both definitions reported to check robustness of conclusions to the OOD definition].
- (c) Diversity-collapse indicator (ADDED per refinement): duplicate/mode-collapse rate — (i) exact-canonical-SMILES duplicate rate, (ii) unique-fraction among valid molecules, (iii) scaffold-level collapse: fraction of generations mapping to the top-10 Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, and (iv) internal diversity (mean pairwise Tanimoto on a sample). Property feedback's classic failure is mode collapse; this is measured directly, not inferred.
- Composite hallucination score reported but not used for the headline conclusion (headline uses the three components separately to avoid masking trade-offs).

3.3 Structural diversity metrics
- Carbon chain-length distribution: distribution of longest continuous carbon chain (and a distribution of total n-carbon counts) per arm; explicit test of the "ultra-long chain over-representation" claim: compare the upper-tail mass of Arm B vs Arm A vs the reference set (e.g., P(chain length ≥ 12), plus quantile comparison). This directly tests whether feedback reduces or worsens ultra-long-chain bias.
- Scaffold diversity: number of unique Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, scaffold Shannon entropy / Simpson index vs reference.
- Tanimoto spread: distribution of pairwise internal Tanimoto similarity and nearest-neighbor-to-reference Tanimoto (alignment measure).

4. ANALYSIS PLAN

4.1 Paired comparisons
- Per seed i, compute Δ_i = metric(B_i) − metric(A_i) for every endpoint. Report paired mean/median Δ with bootstrap CIs (resample seeds and molecules within seed; cluster bootstrap by seed to respect dependence). Primary paired test: seed-paired Wilcoxon signed-rank as nonparametric primary, with sign and effect size (paired Cliff's delta) reported; no reliance on normality.

4.2 Distributional alignment tests
- Two-sample tests of generated vs reference distributions: Kolmogorov–Smirnov on each scalar property and chain length; Maximum Mean Discrepancy (RBF kernel) on the joint property vector (p-logP, QED, MW, chain length) for multivariate alignment. MMD computed with a fixed kernel bandwidth chosen on the reference set only (pre-registered choice), identical for both arms.
- Alignment verdict per arm: closer alignment = smaller KS statistic / MMD. Report per feedback strength so we can see whether stronger feedback moves closer on properties but farther on diversity — the trade-off curve.

4.3 Validity-adjusted gains
- Primary property endpoint is the validity-adjusted aggregate (§3.1); the unadjusted mean is secondary. If feedback "wins" only on unadjusted metrics while validity drops, that is reported as a failure mode, not a success.

4.4 Diversity–property trade-off analysis
- For each feedback strength β and iteration count T: plot (property gain vs Arm A) against (diversity retention: unique fraction, scaffold count, upper-tail chain-length mass). Expected form: a frontier. Conclusion is stated as "feedback improves properties at feedback strength s while retaining ≥ x% of baseline diversity" — conditional, never unconditional.
- Direction-neutral decision rule (pre-specified): feedback is judged beneficial ONLY IF (i) validity-adjusted properties improve significantly, (ii) OOD rate does not increase, (iii) collapse indicators do not degrade beyond a pre-set tolerance (e.g., unique fraction stays ≥ 90% of baseline), and (iv) ultra-long-chain upper-tail mass does not exceed the reference set's. Any other pattern — including a null result or diversity collapse — is reported as such. The design detects improvement, null, and degradation symmetrically.

4.5 Sensitivity analyses
- Reward weights perturbation (§1.3); OOD-definition perturbation (§3.2b); affinity surrogate swap (if two surrogates available) to check conclusions are surrogate-robust.

5. FEASIBILITY

- Compute: entirely CPU-only. All scoring (p-logP, QED, validity, Tanimoto, scaffolds) is standard cheminformatics computation on generated structures; the surrogate affinity is a pre-computed model or a fixed docking configuration run offline. 224 CPUs are more than sufficient; no GPU, no network needed. Runtime estimate [ASSUMPTION]: hours-scale, dominated by generation and pairwise-Tanimoto sampling (internal diversity computed on a fixed random subsample of n=1000 per arm to bound O(n²) cost).
- Dependencies [ASSUMPTION]: RDKit-class toolkit + a pretrained generator + affinity surrogate; none are preinstalled in the current environment (rdkit import fails) — but per track.md, compute and repositories are NOT required for this design-only deliverable, so this does not block the design. If execution were ever commissioned, dependency installation would be a prerequisite step.
- Data: one reference set needs to be available/obtainable; currently absent from the workspace [ASSUMPTION: a public drug-like collection is used].

6. EXPLICIT ASSUMPTION REGISTER (nothing unconfirmed is stated as fact)
All of the following are ASSUMPTIONS, absent from task.json/track.md and from any source:
(a) Base generator framework (§1.2) — unspecified; design is framework-agnostic.
(b) Feedback mechanism form, weights, iteration counts, strength grid (§1.3) — invented for operationalization.
(c) Affinity surrogate and/or receptor (§1.4) — unspecified; one fixed surrogate assumed.
(d) Reference real-world dataset and sampling protocol (§2, §5) — unspecified.
(e) OOD operationalization and thresholds (§3.2b, §4.4 tolerance levels) — unspecified; two definitions reported.
(f) Number of seeds, sample sizes n per arm, subsample sizes for diversity metrics (§2–4) — chosen for CPU feasibility, not source-mandated.
(g) Property definitions (penalized logP, RDKit QED) — standard forms assumed, not source-specified.
(h) Runtime estimate — assumption, not measured.

7. LIMITATIONS
- Proxy affinity only: any affinity surrogate result is a computational proxy against an assumed/fixed target; it supports NO therapeutic claim, no real binding prediction, and no drug-discovery validity. Conclusions are about generator behavior relative to the proxy, not chemistry reality.
- Unknown empirical outcome: the question presupposes feedback helps, but realistic risk is the opposite (high-logP/QED reward pressure collapsing diversity and inflating lipophilicity — exactly the ultra-long-chain failure mode named in the question). The design is deliberately direction-neutral: its decision rule (§4.4) can return "feedback helps", "no effect", or "feedback harms diversity/hallucination", and all three outcomes are equally reportable.
- Proxy-relative conclusions: because the receptor, reference set, and generator are assumptions, conclusions hold within the chosen setup; transferability to other generators/targets is untested and would require the sensitivity analyses in §4.5.
- Design-only: this document specifies the experiment; nothing has been run, and no exploratory command here constitutes evidence about the outcome.

SUMMARY
A seed-paired, budget-matched A/B comparison of a base generator with vs without a p-logP/QED/affinity feedback loop, evaluated on full property distributions, three-component hallucination (validity + OOD + collapse/duplicate rate), and structural diversity (chain-length upper tail, scaffold diversity, Tanimoto spread), with KS/MMD alignment tests, validity-adjusted endpoints, a feedback-strength trade-off sweep, and a pre-specified direction-neutral decision rule. Every operational detail not present in the sources is labeled as an assumption; feasibility is CPU-only and offline, consistent with the design-only contract.

2. CONTROLS

- Matched compute/sampling budget: both arms draw the same number of raw generated molecules and the same number of scoring calls (feedback arm's resampling counts against its budget — no free extra samples).

3.2 Hallucination metrics (three components per researcher refinement)
- (a) Validity rate: fraction of generated SMILES that parse and pass RDKit valence/sanitization.
- (b) Out-of-distribution (OOD) rate: fraction of generated molecules outside the reference real-world distribution [ASSUMPTION: operationalized as (i) nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity to reference set below a threshold AND (ii) multivariate property-vector outlier via distance to reference quantiles; both definitions reported to check robustness of conclusions to the OOD definition].

3.3 Structural diversity metrics
- Carbon chain-length distribution: distribution of longest continuous carbon chain (and a distribution of total n-carbon counts) per arm; explicit test of the "ultra-long chain over-representation" claim: compare the upper-tail mass of Arm B vs Arm A vs the reference set (e.g., P(chain length ≥ 12), plus quantile comparison). - Scaffold diversity: number of unique Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, scaffold Shannon entropy / Simpson index vs reference.
- Tanimoto spread: distribution of pairwise internal Tanimoto similarity and nearest-neighbor-to-reference Tanimoto (alignment measure).

4. ANALYSIS PLAN

4.1 Paired comparisons
- Per seed i, compute Δ_i = metric(B_i) − metric(A_i) for every endpoint. Report paired mean/median Δ with bootstrap CIs (resample seeds and molecules within seed; cluster bootstrap by seed to respect dependence). Primary paired test: seed-paired Wilcoxon signed-rank as nonparametric primary, with sign and effect size (paired Cliff's delta) reported; no reliance on normality.

4.2 Distributional alignment tests
- Two-sample tests of generated vs reference distributions: Kolmogorov–Smirnov on each scalar property and chain length; Maximum Mean Discrepancy (RBF kernel) on the joint property vector (p-logP, QED, MW, chain length) for multivariate alignment. 4.3 Validity-adjusted gains
- Primary property endpoint is the validity-adjusted aggregate (§3.1); the unadjusted mean is secondary. If feedback "wins" only on unadjusted metrics while validity drops, that is reported as a failure mode, not a success.

- For each feedback strength β and iteration count T: plot (property gain vs Arm A) against (diversity retention: unique fraction, scaffold count, upper-tail chain-length mass).
